greeting: Good morning, Bay View, and happy Thanksgiving Eve. It's a gray, quiet Wednesday with a high in the low 40s, and there's no school this week for MPS, St. Thomas Aquinas, Saint Lucas or Downtown Montessori students, so expect the parks and coffee shops to be busy. If you still need anything from the library, today is the day: every Milwaukee Public Library branch is closed Thursday and Friday.

top.title: Radish, a chef's restaurant and market, sets a Dec. 15 opening on Delaware Avenue
top.dek: Bay View native Micaela Erickson's new spot at Delaware and Pryor opens with a holiday menu.
top.body:
Radish, the restaurant and small market from Bay View-raised chef Micaela Erickson, now has an opening date. The business announced on Instagram that it will open Tuesday, Dec. 15, with a special holiday menu, and it shared a first look at a bright dining room with globe lights, a long counter and bentwood stools.

Radish's website lists its home as 2591 S. Delaware Ave., at the corner of Delaware and Pryor avenues. That's a change from the plan Erickson announced in January 2025, when the project was headed for a tiny storefront at 2986 S. Kinnickinnic Ave. The site describes a seasonal menu, a thoughtfully sourced market and low-intervention wines.

Planned hours on the site are 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. Tuesday and Wednesday and 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. Thursday through Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday, with no reservations. Erickson ran a private-chef business, also called Radish, for years and previously cooked at La Merenda, Bavette La Boucherie and Ca'Lucchenzo, according to Urban Milwaukee's 2025 report on the project.

image.alt: Radish's new dining room on Delaware Avenue, with globe lights, a long white counter and wooden stools

top.title: Library branches close Thursday and Friday; here's what's open around Bay View for the holiday
top.dek: Bay View's branch is open until 8 p.m. today; a few local spots post Thanksgiving hours and Wednesday deals.
top.body:
All Milwaukee Public Library locations, including the Bay View branch at 2566 S. Kinnickinnic Ave., will be closed Thursday and Friday for Thanksgiving. Every branch reopens Saturday, and the Bay View branch is open today until 8 p.m. for anyone stocking up on books and movies for the long weekend.

Several neighborhood spots have posted holiday plans. Sugar Maple opens at 4 p.m. Thursday. Calogero's on Bay Street pours pre-Thanksgiving cocktails tonight and is closed Thursday, and Ian's Pizza says all its locations close for the holiday.

For Thanksgiving Eve, Bay View Bowl offers $3 games and $2.50 Hamm's from 6 p.m. to midnight (and Cafe Centraal's all-night happy hour is in today's Buzz).

help.title: Wisconsin reports a third measles death as officials urge vaccine checks before holiday gatherings
help.dek: The state counts 920 cases this year; health officials say indoor holiday gatherings can speed the spread.
help.body:
The Wisconsin Department of Health Services said Tuesday that an adult in Lafayette County has died of measles, the third death in this year's outbreak. Two children in Grant County died earlier this month, the state's first measles deaths since 1990.

The state has logged 920 cases in 2026, including 88 confirmed since Friday, and the outbreak has reached 24 counties. Nearly all cases are in people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown.

With Thanksgiving gatherings and travel this week, health officials are asking people to check their vaccination records. Two doses of the MMR vaccine are about 97% effective, and the state's chief epidemiologist said adults with only one documented dose can safely get a second. Your doctor or pharmacy can check your records.

image.alt: Microscope image of tissue infected with the measles virus

spotlight.title: Spotlight: Hi-Fi Cafe
spotlight.dek: Nearly 30 years of coffee, jukebox tunes and retro decor at the corner of KK and Potter.
spotlight.body:
Hi-Fi Cafe sits in the rounded corner storefront where Kinnickinnic and Potter avenues meet, under a striped awning and a multicolored "HI-FI" sign that has marked that stretch of KK for nearly three decades. It is a counter-service coffeehouse with all-day breakfast, brunch and lunch, and a reputation as one of Bay View's longest-running hangouts.

The cafe opened around 1996 under Sage Schwarm, a Milwaukee musician who played in Wild Kingdom and Citizen King. In 2003 he sold it to Mary Hart and her partner, Peter Frederick Steinhoff, who have run it since. Milwaukee Record's "Mandatory Milwaukee" series profiled it in 2019, and Urban Milwaukee's dining column called it a time warp in 2020.

That label comes from the room itself: Formica and butcher-block tables, red vinyl chairs, neon signs, a vintage magazine rack and a jukebox, plus walls hung with work by local artists. The menu leans vegetarian-friendly and a little playful. Sandwiches carry names like Stringy Iggy (house corned beef), Jean Jeanie (hummus and veggies) and Falafel Yum Yum, and the espresso list includes a Raspberry Beret and a peanut-butter Buttercup. The coffee is Valentine's organic, fair-trade roast, and the quiche and soup change daily.

The past few years have tested the business. A September 2020 GoFundMe raised nearly 2,000, and in spring 2023 the owners launched a second campaign, with a 5,000 goal, to pay for renovations while the cafe was temporarily closed. Hart told Urban Milwaukee it was "the only place like it in Milwaukee, the Midwest" and beyond. Singer Abby Jeanne, a former Hi-Fi employee, also started a small label called Hi-Fi Records, whose first release was a holiday single recorded in the cafe's kitchen.

These days the cafe's Instagram lists it as open Wednesday through Sunday, and it stayed open until 9 p.m. for Bay View Gallery Night in September. It sells e-gift cards through its website. We couldn't find a Thanksgiving weekend schedule, so check its Instagram before heading over.

Hi-Fi Cafe, 2640 S. Kinnickinnic Ave. Open Wednesday through Sunday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Phone 414-486-0504. Website: 5ea646d4d1216.site123.me. Instagram: @hificafemke.

history.title: Lance Sijan: the Bay View High standout who received the Medal of Honor
history.text: In November 1967, Air Force Capt. Lance Sijan, a Bay View High graduate, was shot down over Laos. His courage as a prisoner earned him the Medal of Honor.
history.body:
Lance Peter Sijan grew up in Bay View and was a standout at Bay View High School: senior class president, an all-city end on the football team, and the lead in a school production of "The King and I." He went on to the Air Force Academy, graduated in 1965, and by July 1967 was flying F-4 Phantom missions in the Vietnam War.

On Nov. 9, 1967, his jet went down over Laos. Rescue crews made voice contact with him and hovered overhead, but he was badly injured and warned them off because enemy troops were all around him. Back in Bay View, two Air Force officers came to his family's door with the news that he was missing.

Sijan evaded capture for 46 days, surviving on plants and insects despite a skull fracture, a mangled hand and a broken leg. He was captured on Christmas Day 1967 and taken to a prison camp in Hanoi, where he died on Jan. 22, 1968, at 25. His family didn't learn his fate until 1974, when his remains came home; he is buried in Arlington Park Cemetery in Greenfield.

Fellow prisoners later described his courage, and in 1976 President Gerald Ford posthumously awarded him the Medal of Honor. The Air Force Academy named a dormitory Sijan Hall, the Air Force named its top leadership award for him, and in Bay View, the football field where he practiced was renamed Sijan Park.
